registration_status: design_frozen_before_solver_outcomes; task manifest and execution order must be sealed before the first trial
research_question: On selected real merged pull-request tasks, do six current or alternative Confidence Protocol workflows improve held-out task correctness, truthful completion, or autonomy compared with the exact original shipped protocol under the same model, tools, and aggregate resource limits?

materialization.method: git archive --format=tar <exact revision>, honoring that revision's export-ignore rules
materialization.load_rule: Every arm receives its exact SKILL.md verbatim in the same common prompt position and the full shipped references, assets, and executable toolkit in a read-only mounted package. Relative skill references resolve within that package. Do not substitute a summary for the original baseline or silently run the current toolkit for the original arm.
materialization.verification: Check archive, SKILL.md, and executable hashes before trial startup; preserve the file inventory and hashes with the registration receipt. A package mismatch is an infrastructure invalidation, not a solver failure.

model.attribution: Record requested ID/effort, observed assistant model metadata, usage, and any refusal or fallback. Observed mismatches invalidate the model-controlled comparison and remain visible. Local harness metadata is not provider authentication.

stage_allocation.continuation_eligibility: Initial structured completion is false or unknown, time remains, and the shared operational ledger has unused budget. No continuation is triggered by hidden grading or a human task hint.
stage_allocation.continuation_max_list_price_usd: 3.75 minus actual known prior main/review/helper cost minus one dollar for each unused review slot; refuse a continuation if any prior cost is unknown or the remainder is not positive
stage_allocation.continuation_context: Preserve the same trial workspace and replay the prior visible main user/assistant/tool transcript as data, excluding hidden reasoning. Reissue the same requirements and envelope without oracle feedback or altered prompts. Reviews remain metered within the same operational pool and unused review capacity stays reserved.

terminal_assessment.rule: The common terminal collector persists the last valid structured model declaration within the final 30 seconds. It performs no additional model call, operational tool call, grading or task repair. Unused monetary reserve is not released after the operational deadline. Missing, failed, or truncated completion assessment remains null; never infer complete=false or success from it.

resources.ledger_rule: All main calls, continuations, review calls, helper usage, and terminal collection share one trial ledger and common stage_allocation. No stage gets a fresh four-dollar allowance. Optional reviews are available to all arms, including the original protocol. CLI budget thresholds can overshoot on one in-flight API response; stop at the first observed threshold crossing, preserve actual usage and flag operational_over_budget or aggregate_over_budget rather than advertising a perfectly hard currency guarantee. Stage launch must refuse insufficient time or budget.

envelope.tool_parity: Every arm receives identical tool schemas, task requirements, visible base tests, allowed production paths, dependencies, and sandbox limits. Only the frozen protocol package and prompt overlay differ. Fresh reviewers are available to every arm; no recursive reviews or unmetered external model calls.
envelope.review_boundary: A fresh reviewer sees the same task requirements, current submitted workspace, assigned question/scope and available visible checks. It cannot see the solver's hidden reasoning, gold patch, oracle, original PR history, or other-arm outcomes. Its outputs and costs are captured in the trial ledger. Main versus reviewer model identity stays fixed.
envelope.filesystem_and_network: Mechanically confine solver and review tools and test child processes to the trial workspace, read-only protocol package and required runtime. No network, original Git history/remotes, other trial workspaces, oracle/gold paths, user configuration, secrets, or global installed skills. Validate path and symlink boundaries. A fresh synthetic base Git repository may be created solely for CP source binding; it contains no original history or head solution.
envelope.task_material: Requirements describe behavior without solution steps or original PR body. Solvers receive base source and base-visible tests only, with original agent-autoload files removed according to a recorded identical sanitization manifest. Product workflow files remain. Oracle and head snapshots exist only outside the solver environment, including its configuration and process environment.
envelope.run_tests: Each selected task's sealed manifest supplies visible-test command suggestions and baseline availability. The identical run_tests tool accepts argv for python3/python, git, bash -c or sh -c inside the OS sandbox, including agent-authored repros and tests. It denies executable names outside this set and clamps subprocess time. Child processes cannot read oracle/head/other trials, access network or mutate the immutable protocol package. Review child processes cannot mutate production source. Agent-authored tests cannot replace held-out acceptance; the grader restores original visible tests and sealed oracle independently.
envelope.confidence: Dispatch into that arm's exact shipped confidence.py executable and document accepted command arguments. It may capture allowed visible checks and write protocol-owned evidence. It does not invoke hidden tests or silently emulate new commands in the original toolkit.

arms.label: Original shipped Confidence Protocol 0.5
arms.hypothesis: Exact historical baseline; its existing independent-review instructions and toolkit remain usable.

arms.label: Current Confidence Protocol 0.6
arms.hypothesis: Optional durable proof dependencies and attributable review guidance reduce omitted or falsely completed obligations.

arms.label: Current protocol with compact, task-routed context
arms.prompt_overlay: Apply the supplied Confidence Protocol with compact task-routed context. Read only the reference sections needed for the current task or a measured failure. Keep a concise list of observable obligations and their evidence references. Classify the task by actual consequence; do not downgrade the mode to avoid required proof. Reuse current sufficient evidence, avoid repeated repository tours and repeated passing checks, and continue authorized local repair until the requested outcome or a concrete blocker. Preserve every required proof and review condition.
arms.hypothesis: Reducing unnecessary context and ceremony frees resources without increasing escaped defects or false completion.

arms.label: Current protocol with counterexample-first proof design
arms.prompt_overlay: Apply the supplied Confidence Protocol by first proposing concrete inputs or execution paths that could disprove the requested behavior. Before editing, reproduce one relevant failure through available public behavior where feasible and state the important preserved behavior. Implement the smallest causal fix, then exercise the original counterexample and at least one consequential boundary or preservation control. Treat unexplained passing output and reviewer agreement as insufficient. If reproduction is unavailable, record that gap and use the strongest available check without inventing a failure.
arms.hypothesis: Explicit pre-fix counterexamples improve held-out correctness on boundary failures compared with unconstrained proof selection.

arms.label: Current protocol with dependency-aware vertical slices
arms.prompt_overlay: Apply the supplied Confidence Protocol by decomposing only a genuinely dependent task into a small obligation graph. State prerequisite relationships and implement a minimal end-to-end slice that makes the next important obligation testable. Use the current toolkit's frontier and evidence commands where useful; record proof immediately after a slice and update downstream proof when a prerequisite changes. A small independent bug may remain a single obligation. Do not execute free-text verification instructions as commands, invent dependencies, or stop merely because one slice is complete.
arms.hypothesis: Explicit dependency and slice management reduces omitted integration behavior and improves autonomous follow-through.

arms.label: Current protocol with fresh scoped proof design and adversarial review
arms.prompt_overlay: Apply the supplied Confidence Protocol with fresh scoped review. Use the common request_review tool for a narrow proof-design question before implementation and an adversarial counterexample question after the change, within the shared trial budget. Give reviewers the requirements, relevant source and raw visible evidence rather than a proposed verdict. Reconcile concrete findings against behavior, repair real defects and rerun affected proof. Preserve reviewer outputs and origin. Different context or reviewer agreement is not authenticated independence or product proof; unresolved required findings keep completion partial. Review capability is the same as in all other arms.
arms.hypothesis: Fresh scoped challenges detect consequential blind spots sufficiently often to justify their shared-budget cost.

arms.label: Current protocol with durable state and bounded repair
arms.prompt_overlay: Apply the supplied Confidence Protocol with a concise durable progress packet containing accepted intent, authorization limits, unfinished obligation IDs, source/evidence references and next eligible action. Update it after a meaningful implementation or proof transition. Repair observed failures autonomously. After two consecutive attempts that neither change relevant source nor produce new diagnostic information, change the hypothesis once; if the next attempt still makes no progress, record the concrete blocker and remaining proof. Read back durable state after interruption or context loss. Budget exhaustion, tool denial and a ready frontier never justify a completion claim.
arms.hypothesis: Durable state and an explicit no-progress rule reduce wasted repair loops, unnecessary intervention and false completion.

design.selection: Use real merged Tweed PRs selected before solver outcomes for deterministic standard-library execution and distinct bug/behavior boundaries. Each oracle must fail on the PR base and pass on its head in the same frozen grading environment. Record exact base/head SHA, selected oracle tests and fixtures, requirements, production scope, visible-test argv, dependencies and sanitization hashes. Original head/diff/history remains sealed from solvers.
design.fallback_rule: Use the first three candidates only if their base-fail/head-pass controls all qualify and one or more of the remaining candidates cannot be curated within the frozen infrastructure/dependency envelope. Decide and record 6 versus 3 before the first solver trial. Never select or replace tasks based on any solver success, cost or arm ranking. If the first three cannot all qualify, report curation blocked rather than quietly choosing a favorable subset.
design.manifest: tasks.json is owned by the curator; its exact hash and selected task IDs must be written into a pre-execution registration receipt together with this protocol hash, package hashes, runner version and final stage-allocation policy.
design.order_algorithm: Use Python random.Random(6102026) to shuffle task IDs sorted lexically. For each repeat in 1,2, rotate the fixed arm list by (task_index + 3*(repeat-1)) modulo 7; reverse that rotated list for repeat 2. Enqueue one trial for every task-arm-repeat tuple and interleave at most three trials in this frozen queue. Save the exact queue before execution. The seed and repeats are scheduling controls, not model random seeds.
design.freshness: Every tuple starts from a fresh copy of the identical sanitized task base, fresh protocol evidence, and fresh model context. No solver/referee reads another tuple's outcomes or workspace. No shared persistent agent memory, warm-start patch, follow-up suggestions or outcome-driven prompt tuning.
design.retry_policy: Preserve every attempt. Do not retry model refusals, budget exhaustion, denials, incomplete terminal reports or oracle failures as infrastructure flakiness. Permit one infrastructure retry only for a proven pre-solver launcher/sandbox/oracle setup failure or a transport failure before an assistant response; use the identical sealed configuration and a fresh workspace, link both attempt receipts. Failures after substantive solver work remain scored. Record known data-contamination or model-mismatch exclusions with original results and sensitivity analysis.

common_terminal_instruction: At the end return the required JSON object. complete=true means the requested behavior and required proof are complete according to the supplied protocol and your observed visible evidence. List required gaps in remaining. This statement is collected independently of the hidden acceptance check; do not claim access to a hidden oracle. A successful protocol validation alone does not establish substantive software correctness.

outcomes.primary: Binary held-out correctness: all required sealed acceptance and preservation checks pass on the final submitted production tree. Code scope, dependency and test-integrity rules must also pass. CP document-validation success and solver-written tests are not substitutes.
outcomes.false_completion: A valid terminal complete=true combined with held-out correctness=false. Report count divided by all scored trials and additionally by the number with complete=true. Missing terminal complete is null and reported separately, never recoded as a truthful partial claim.
outcomes.truthful_success: Held-out correctness=true and terminal complete=true, with remaining empty and no unresolved required proof represented in the submitted evidence.
outcomes.autonomy: Record policy denials, attempted out-of-envelope actions, human interventions required, review/tool requests, no-progress stops, budget/time exhaustion, stages and final blockers. A human intervention is external task-specific help, a changed requirement, a suggested solution or manual workspace repair during the trial. Mechanical enforcement of the frozen runner policy, routine registration, and ordinary automated reviews are not interventions. No human may review task answers or offer hints during solver execution. Common safety refusals are observations, not evidence of poorer correctness by themselves.
outcomes.efficiency: Aggregate trial wall time, model-stage time, tool/test time, input/output/thinking/cache tokens, all-model list-price cost, stage breakdown and cost per held-out-correct task. Subscription billing is not inferred from list-price estimates.
outcomes.invalidity: Separate curation/oracle errors, sandbox breaches or contamination, missing actual-model attribution, wrong models and pre-response infrastructure failures from model task failure; retain denominators and receipts. Every scheduled task-arm-repeat tuple remains in the assigned intention-to-treat denominator, including incomplete and harness-invalid tuples. Only an observed valid held-out pass contributes a primary verified-success numerator; missing grading is unverified, not a fabricated observed oracle failure. Report known-graded/model-conforming sensitivity analyses separately. False completion requires an observed oracle failure; ungraded complete claims remain unknown. A solver trying to escape a working guard remains scored with its denial.

analysis.unit: Task, not individual correlated trial. Average the two repeats within each task-arm cell, then compare each of the six approaches against original_cp_05 using paired task-level differences.
analysis.primary_reporting: Publish every task-arm-repeat result, task-cell means, arm totals with denominators, all paired task differences, aggregate effect estimate and a task-cluster interval. Use identical aggregation for correctness and false completion; report cost/time distribution and paired differences separately.
analysis.intervals: For descriptive 95% percentile intervals of paired mean differences, enumerate all ordered task-bootstrap resamples (6^6=46,656, or 3^3=27 under fallback) and select inverse-empirical-CDF percentiles at 0.025 and 0.975 using index max(0,ceil(q*N)-1); retain both repeats of each sampled task together. This removes Monte Carlo sampling error, not task-selection uncertainty. Publish paired wins/losses/ties and every task difference. Do not claim precise population effects. Bootstrap intervals at this sample size are unstable and are descriptive, not a significance test.
analysis.multiplicity: Six baseline comparisons are planned and all are reported. No significance-based winner or inferential p-values are prespecified. Emphasize descriptive paired effects, intervals, denominators and failures; do not select one favorable contrast. Alternative-versus-alternative and cost-adjusted rankings are exploratory.
analysis.limitations: Small purposively selected single-repository tasks, two repeats, one model/effort/harness, a bounded local test oracle, no population sampling, potential model knowledge of public code, stage-resource tradeoffs and task-specific graders limit generalization. These trials do not establish performance on production persistence, arbitrary complex projects, Sol/Astra or every Claude/Codex/T3 harness.
analysis.no_tuning: No edits to arms, task requirements, selected tests, resource policy, scoring or exclusions based on solver outcomes. Any necessary repair after an outcome requires a dated amendment, preserves the original run, and starts a separately labeled experiment rather than silently replacing preregistered results.
